Saved. Summary of what I learned and recorded:

This was a genuinely new question category (CPI-U inflation adjustment), so a skill update was warranted.

Key insight: My answer (48954.4) vs gold (56117.5) was off by a clean constant factor of 1.146 — independent of any plausible CPI rate. That signature means the inflation arithmetic was correct and I read the wrong Treasury base value. Backing out the implied base: gold needs ~53,227M but I read ~46,433M for "total currency in circulation." That ~13% gap is the classic symptom of grabbing a partial/sub-total row (Federal Reserve notes only, or currency-outside-banks) instead of the grand-total "total currency in circulation" line in the money-stock exhibit.

What I saved:
- Skill: New section "CPI-U inflation-adjustment wrapper" with the formula (adjusted = V*(1+r), r = YoY same calendar month one year apart), the "applying the rate = inflate, not deflate" clarification, the clean-constant-factor diagnostic for wrong-base-row detection, and the specific "TOTAL currency in circulation = grand-total row" guidance. Reference CPI-U values (Nov1968=36.8, Nov1969=38.8).
- Memory: Compact pointer with the formula, the inflate-not-deflate rule, and the wrong-row diagnostic, fitting it in by tightening an existing entry.
